positions.as_written: Where it is contested: whether a grade three medial injury alongside an ACL tear should be reconstructed, braced, or left.
Read a medial sectioning study's dissection boundary before its attribution, since the boundary is a judgement rather than a given.
Treat quantified anatomical positions as targets with ranges rather than as fixed points.
Read the healing literature separately from the mechanical literature and do not let the strength of the second lend credibility to the first.
Read rotation results only where the coordinate system is stated.
Take the patient's age and physiology into account, since healing capacity is the whole argument for waiting and it is not uniform.
Take comorbidities into account, because stiffness after medial surgery is more likely in some of them.
Take the demands on the knee into account, since rotational demand is what residual medial laxity actually troubles.
Take the psychological state into account, because a staged plan requires a patient who can tolerate an interval of uncertainty.
Decide on the balance, state it, and record what would change it.
Read the rotation work before the valgus work, because rotation is where the management argument actually lives.
